elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and disclaims any non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 affirmatively permits competing activities rather than restricting them.
Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory, and §12.4 imposes no field or territorial prohibition.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a named competing product.
elements.evidence: No operative restriction remains, so the condition requiring a restriction to be confined to a named product is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: There is no operative restriction during or after the term. The 24-month language in §12.4 qualifies an affirmative permission, not a prohibition.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction exists, so its effective duration is zero and does not exceed 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer’s internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly leaves Customer unrestricted in developing any product or service, and §12.4 also affirmatively permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly leaves Customer unrestricted in acquiring any product or service, and §12.4 affirmatively permits acquisition of competing products or services.

result.reason: The one-word operator change removes the non-compete and, together with §12.3, reaches the preferred position without changing unrelated commercial terms. The result is operative but poor drafting: §12.4 is redundant, retains an unnecessary territorial reference and 24-month period, and could create avoidable negative-implication ambiguity about Customer’s freedom after that period. Deleting §12.4 would be materially clearer.
